_meta.why_this_file: data/layouts.json is regenerated wholesale by tools/layouts.py from MM2_RE_KIT/.../_ALL_TYPES.h, which does not contain these classes, and tools/build.py re-runs tools/genheaders.py on every build. Without a layout here, a regeneration silently strips the members out of matrix33.h and matrix66.h and matrix33.cpp stops compiling. This file is how the derived layout survives that cycle: re-merge with tools/merge_layouts.py --write.

data/symbols.json - the linker map, for symbol-to-address binding; all 28 Matrix33 and Matrix66 symbols are functions, there is no static and no vftable in either class

Matrix33.note: Three independent witnesses for the size, and no member is inferred - every one of the nine is written by ?Set@Matrix33@@QAEXABV1@@Z. SIZE: (1) ?Set@Matrix33@@QAEXABV1@@Z at 0x496230 copies exactly nine dwords through edx, +0x00 through +0x20, then `pop ebp; ret 4` - it stops at 0x24. (2) ?Inverse@Matrix33@@QAEXABV1@@Z at 0x4969D0 makes room for one local with `sub esp, 0x24`. (3) ?Inverse@Matrix33@@QAEXXZ at 0x4968B0 copies its result home with `mov ecx, 9; lea esi, [ebp-0x2c]; rep movsd`. ALL NINE SLOTS ARE FLOATS: ?Add@Matrix33@@QAEXABV1@@Z (0x496270) is nine fld/fadd/fstp dword triples over the same nine offsets, and ?Negate@Matrix33@@QAEXXZ (0x4967F0) is nine fld/fchs/fstp dword triples. NAMES ARE ROW-MAJOR, matching Matrix34: ?Dot@Matrix33@@QAEXABV1@@Z (0x496490) is instruction-for-instruction ?Dot3x3@Matrix34@@QAEXABV1@@Z, whose member names come from the IDB, over the identical nine offsets; and ?CrossProduct@Matrix33@@QAEXABVVector3@@@Z (0x496750) writes -z,y,z,-x,-y,x into +0x04,+0x08,+0x0C,+0x14,+0x18,+0x1C, which is the skew matrix of `arg1 % v` under this reading and its negation under the transposed one.

Matrix66.note: Four Matrix33 blocks and nothing else. Every one of the eleven Matrix66 bodies (0x496A00-0x496ECF) is a fixed sequence of `lea ecx, [reg + block]` followed by a call into Matrix33, and the only four block values that ever appear are 0x00, 0x24, 0x48 and 0x6C - no body touches a float or any other offset. SIZE: ?Inverse@Matrix66@@QAEXXZ at 0x496D00 allocates a whole one with `sub esp, 0x90`, and ?Set@Matrix66@@QAEXABV1@@Z (0x496A00) passes arg+0x00/+0x24/+0x48/+0x6C as the four arguments of ?Set@Matrix66@@QAEXABVMatrix33@@000@Z, which stores them to this+0x00/+0x24/+0x48/+0x6C - the four blocks tile 0x90 exactly with no gap. See the per-member evidence for which block is which.

members.name: m00
members.evidence: ?Dot@Matrix66@@QAEXABV1@@Z (0x496B80) builds the first result block as (this+0x00 * arg1+0x00) + (this+0x24 * arg1+0x48) - the 2x2 block product C00 = A00*B00 + A01*B10.

members.name: m01
members.evidence: the second operand of that same product, so +0x24 is the (0,1) block; ?Transpose@Matrix66@@QAEXABV1@@Z (0x496CC0) independently fills +0x24 from arg1+0x48.

members.name: m10
members.evidence: ?Transpose@Matrix66@@QAEXABV1@@Z fills +0x48 from arg1+0x24, the mirror of the line above; ?Dot@Matrix66 uses it as the (1,0) block.

members.name: m11
members.evidence: ?Transpose@Matrix66@@QAEXXZ (0x496C70) transposes +0x00 and +0x6C in place and swaps +0x24 with +0x48, so +0x00 and +0x6C are the diagonal blocks.
